summary: Duplicate Machine SID after depot reimage causes MECM policy flap and intermittent AAD join failures
description: Issue summary: Several devices returned from depot repair are exhibiting repeated MECM client policy oscillation and failing AAD hybrid join intermittently. Suspected root cause is duplicate Machine SID left on disk image leading to identity collisions in on-prem inventory and policy evaluation.
impact: Multiple users (approx 12 devices observed) unable to complete policy-driven provisioning steps. Affected machines receive conflicting MECM assignments causing service config churn, blocking application deployment and onboarding checks. No external customer impact, internal fleet only.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Reimage device using depot standard image produced on 2026-03-05 build
2) Run sysprep/clone sequence used by depot team (observed step that preserves SID),
3) Device checks into MECM and attempts Hybrid AAD join
4) Observe MECM client policy flipping between 'CompanyResourceConfig' and 'WorkstationBaseline' every ~5-10 minutes
5) Hybrid AAD join often times out or reports 'device already exists' during token exchange
observed_behavior: MECM client shows rapid policy re-evaluation. AAD join fails with HTTP 409 / deviceConflict or times out after retries. Inventory in assetdb shows duplicated machine_identifier and identical machine SID values for two different asset tags (one repaired unit and another active unit).
expected_behavior: Each reimaged device should receive a fresh, unique Machine SID and stable MECM policy assignment. Hybrid AAD join should complete on first attempt and device should appear once in assetdb with correct asset tag.
logs_snippets: MECM client log: PolicyAgent::EvaluatePolicy - lastPolicyId=abc123 newPolicyId=def456 (flip)
AAD join log: HybridJoinService - 409 DeviceConflict: existingDeviceId=asset-49321 incomingDeviceId=asset-50218
imaging script output: sysprep step skipped due to marker file /var/local/skip_sysprep (unexpected)
assetdb: machine_sid= S-1-5-21-1122334455-66778899-10101010 appears on asset-49321 and asset-50218
investigation_notes: Initial triage by onsite depot engineer confirmed that a custom disk preparation hook was introduced in the 2026-03-05 image that avoids SID regeneration for perceived faster provisioning. We identified a 'skip_sysprep' marker being created by a deprecated OEM script during NVMe firmware update step. Cross-checked assetdb historical records and found collisions between devices that had overlapping manufacturing serial batches.
hypothesis: OEM provisioning hook intended to accelerate imaging inadvertently bypasses sysprep/SID reset when NVMe firmware flash completes. That leaves duplicate SIDs in the fleet causing MECM and AAD identity collisions.
temporary_workaround: 1) Quarantine affected devices by moving them to MECM collection 'Repair-Quarantine' which disables automated deployments until SID reset.
workaround_steps: 1) Boot device to WinPE, run 'sysprep /generalize' to regenerate Machine SID and re-run OOBE
2) Re-enroll device into MECM and re-run hybrid join script
3) Confirm unique machine_sid in assetdb and stable policy assignment for 1 hour
next_steps: 1) Suspend deployment of 2026-03-05 imaging build and audit other recent images for skip_sysprep marker
2) File PR to imaging-scripts to remove OEM 'fast-nvme' hook and ensure sysprep always runs after firmware flashes
3) Run fleet-wide scan query in assetdb to locate duplicate machine_sid entries and schedule remediation
4) Update depot runbook to include SID validation post-repair
5) Notify service desk and depot teams and schedule a hotfix window
